# Data and AI engineering

<!-- Generated by scripts/package/render_roles.py. Edit the YAML source, not this file. -->

**Department id:** `data-ai`  
**Mission:** Use data and models where they beat deterministic software, with evaluations, privacy, cost control and guardrails.

## Startup stage

Usually the backend engineer with an evaluation spreadsheet. The non-negotiables are a representative test set before shipping a model feature and a cost ceiling per feature.

## Agents operating in this department

`data-ai-engineer`, `cto-technology`

## Roles

### Data engineer

Role id: `data-engineer`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Build reliable, governed data pipelines. |
| Scope of responsibility | Ingestion, transformation, lineage, quality, retention, access. |
| Core activities | Inventory sources and rights; Build validated pipelines; Define lineage and deletion propagation |
| Inputs | Data sources; Requirements; Data classification |
| Outputs and deliverables | Pipelines; Data catalogue; Quality checks |
| Decisions it can make | Pipeline design |
| Decisions requiring approval | Use of personal or third-party data |
| Collaborating roles | backend; security; legal |
| Reporting relationship | engineering-lead |
| KPIs | Data quality incidents; Freshness; Deletion SLA |
| Quality expectations | Rights and consent recorded per source |
| Tools and resources | Data catalogue template |
| Common failure modes | Training or retrieval over data without rights; Silent schema drift |
| Appropriate AI autonomy | propose |
| Human approval requirements | Personal data |

### AI engineer

Role id: `ai-engineer`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Integrate models safely with structured outputs, constrained tools and evaluations. |
| Scope of responsibility | Model selection, prompts, tool use, retrieval, guardrails, evaluation, monitoring, cost. |
| Core activities | Compare deterministic vs model; Evaluate candidates on representative set; Build guardrails and fallbacks; Monitor drift and cost |
| Inputs | Task definition; Test set; Privacy requirements |
| Outputs and deliverables | AI design; Eval report; Prompt and model versions; Cost model |
| Decisions it can make | Design within policy |
| Decisions requiring approval | Vendor and data-rights decisions by CTO; consequential automated decisions need human oversight design |
| Collaborating roles | architecture; security; product |
| Reporting relationship | engineering-lead |
| KPIs | Task success on eval set; Cost per request; Incidents |
| Quality expectations | Model output treated as untrusted; eval before ship |
| Tools and resources | Eval template |
| Common failure modes | AI where rules suffice; Benchmark mismatch; Prompt injection; Cost surprises |
| Appropriate AI autonomy | propose |
| Human approval requirements | Vendor; data rights |
